resolutions: The intended possessor selects a monadic or dyadic State structure; formula type is not a separate user choice.
The possessive-state subject reuses Lesson 12 person morphs but has its own automatically selected number connectors.
Singular or common possessive subjects use uh, hui, or zero; plural subjects use hu-an, with supportive i and spelling derived automatically.
Reciprocal ne is a possessor rather than an object and requires a third-person subject.
Nonspecific te is human; nonspecific tla is nonhuman and requires relational or separately authorized compatibility.
Specific possessors always put person in st1, while st2 supplies whichever category st1 does not contain.
First- and second-person possessive o is replaced by square zero before a vowel-initial nounstem.
Third-person possessor number is automatic: zero is singular or common, while m or n is plural according to its licensed boundary.
NNC am-o and VNC am-m-o may look similar in traditional spelling but remain different typed grammatical structures.
